hook.en: In the board exam the composition is the longest single answer. Students who plan, pace and proofread consistently score well, whatever topic they pick.

objectives.en: Divide exam time between choosing, planning, writing and checking
Avoid the common faults examiners report
Write strong openings and endings quickly

narration.en: In the board exam the composition is the longest single answer. Students who plan, pace and proofread consistently score well, whatever topic they pick.

body.en: Treat the composition as four jobs: choose (read every topic, mark its kind), plan (points in order, opening idea, closing idea), write (paragraph by paragraph, watching the time), and check (spelling, agreement, tense, punctuation). A useful split is about a tenth of the time to choose and plan, most of it to write, and the last few minutes to proofread. Keep to the word limit stated in the question paper; going far over it wastes time and invites errors, while falling well short leaves ideas undeveloped.

body.en: Good openings are quick: start with action or dialogue (narrative), a striking image (descriptive), a clear statement of position or a surprising fact (argumentative), or a personal moment (reflective). Avoid dictionary definitions and "In this essay I will". Good endings round off: a resolution with a final image, a return to the opening idea, a final reasoned judgement, or a reflection on what was learnt. Do not introduce a new argument or end with a moral tacked on for no reason.

points.en: Open with action, image, position or moment
Close by resolving or returning to the opening
No new points at the end

text.en: "Don't open that door," my brother whispered, and of course I did.
In this essay I am going to write about my favourite festival.
According to the dictionary, friendship means a relationship between friends.
Every year, India loses more topsoil than it can rebuild in a century.
Festivals are very nice and everyone likes them very much.
The smell of wet earth always takes me back to my grandfather's farm.

explanation.en: Strong openings pull the reader in with action, a fact or an image; weak ones announce, define or say something vague.

problem.en: Plan, in five minutes, a composition on "The value of silence in a noisy world" (reflective).

steps.en: Opening: a moment of noise at a traffic signal, then sudden silence in a library.
Point 1: silence helps us think and listen to ourselves.
Point 2: silence in conversation lets others speak; listening as respect.
Point 3: the world sells noise (notifications, ads); choosing silence is a skill.
Close: return to the library: silence is not empty but full.

answer.en: A reflective plan with a personal frame, three ideas that build, and a closing return to the opening image.
